points.description: States that the prototype program simulates the behaviour of the software product (it acts out or imitates how the product behaves). Equivalent wording such as 'mimics how the system will work' or 'imitates the intended software's behaviour' earns the mark.

States that the simulation covers portions (parts or key features) of the desired software product, not necessarily the whole product. Equivalent wording such as 'only some parts of the final system' earns the mark.

deductions.description: Describing the prototype as a full or finished version of the product, or as the final working software, contradicts the idea of simulation.

rubric.notes: Full marks for saying a prototype simulates how part of the intended software behaves. Award 3 marks for the core idea of simulating behaviour and 2 marks for recognising that only portions of the product are simulated. A vague answer such as 'it helps solve problems' earns no marks.
